findings.issue: The turn-fold and turn-call texts pull in opposite directions. turn-facing-a-bet-fold says the pot 'has grown enough that many pairs and draws are worth a call'. The turn-call justification says 'the doubled bet size raises the required equity; calls that were fine on the flop become losing calls'. Neither is exactly how the grades are produced. The price is bet/(pot+bet), and because the pot grows too, it barely moves from flop to turn. What really changes is that a draw has one card to come instead of two, so its equity is about halved.
findings.evidence: Spec §5 rows turn-facing-a-bet-fold and turn-facing-a-bet-call; docs/advice/postflop-rules.md pot-odds-call and implied-odds-call. The JSON matches the approved spec text word for word, so this is a content note and does not break the spec.
findings.fix: If the user revisits Q-2: base the turn-call justification on draws losing a card (one card to come, so less equity at the same price) instead of on required equity going up. Optionally soften the turn-fold fix to 'a pair or a strong draw is often worth a call'.

findings.issue: The flop-call fix says call only when your chance to win 'beats the price'. The pot-odds-call rule calls when equity is at least the price, with an exact tie counting as a call. The implied-odds-call rule also calls draws slightly below the plain price. 'counting your outs' only hints at that.
findings.evidence: docs/advice/postflop-rules.md rules pot-odds-call ('at least') and implied-odds-call.
findings.fix: Optional wording: '...when your chance to win, counting your outs, covers the price of the call...'.

findings.issue: The flop-bet fix says 'check the rest to see the turn for free'. A check only guarantees a free turn when the hero is last to act; the check-free rule makes no such claim.
findings.fix: Optional: 'check the rest' or 'check the rest and let the turn come cheaply'.

findings.issue: The spec's scope budget is files=12, lines=950. The gate reports 13 changed files and 1228 changed lines. The extra file is the 1-line unlocked test edit, and the extra lines are tests and docs, not new behaviour.
findings.fix: No code change needed. Record the overage in the build log or judge notes. Do not cut tests to fit the budget.

summary: Every SPEC item is implemented as written and the tests would catch a broken implementation. The JSON text matches spec §5 exactly. Each postflop ActionType maps to exactly one of the 15 ids: fold, call and raise count as facing a bet; check and bet do not; preflop gives null. Hinted decisions are skipped before counting. The leak rule is 'decisions >= 8 && 5*errors >= 2*decisions' (integer arithmetic). The tests cover 8/3, 8/4, 10/4, 20/8 and 7/7, plus both hinted cases from AC#6. parseLeakCounts checks known categories in strictly increasing data order, 1 <= decisions, 0 <= errors <= decisions and 0 <= major <= errors. Every bound has a failing case in the test. The unlocked edit to tests/table/session-report-errors.test.ts widens the key-order check from slice(-2) to slice(-3) and drops no assertion, as qa.md's build note says. No src/engine, src/bots, src/advice or src/storage changes. The 5 affected Vitest files pass (15 tests). Only content notes and a scope-budget overage remain; no BLOCKER or MAJOR.
